serious_competing_readings.whole_rival_argument: **“The prize was the real motive, so musical desire is only decoration.”** Semla actually changes peer response and remains a wanted prospective reward. Airi explicitly says it was an added justification; Yoshimi wants a skill, Kazusa wants a record and Natsu values the finite common goal. The stronger account keeps food and music as different goods distributed across people, rather than making the false semla diagnosis true or erasing the peers' appetite after exposing it. [A:L158,L168–180,L202–204,L216,L231; P:L439]

**“Airi must become useful to deserve her place.”** She describes real difficulty and fears abandonment after an offer to be covered. The peers refuse a technically better replacement because they want her at their festival. Founderhood and equality complicate the idea that she has been a passive burden. Those positives do not deny her own wish for ability; they deny that technical indispensability is the condition of her being wanted. [A:L174–180,L251]

**“Role acceptance means every assignment was freely chosen.”** Later effort, actual confidence and pleasure give acceptance substantial evidence. The initial casual procedure meets Yoshimi's objection, Kazusa did not choose vocalist and adult access to unfinished work is explicitly refused. Participation can become meaningful without changing the history of how it was allocated or giving unlimited permission. This reading must keep both real work and specific nonassent. [A:L160,L166; P:L428,L442]

**“The teacher engineers a complete cure.”** Studio help, searches, listening and recognition are actual. Initial misunderstanding, Tsumugi's own challenge, peer initiative, private fear and two significant recipient failures—practice intrusion and forced disclosure—prevent an omniscient or uniformly adequate plan. Airi's local self-liking is a consequential ending, not evidence every skill, future insecurity or relationship has been repaired. [A:L158–180,L197–201]

**“Technical progress makes recipient limits irrelevant.”** More skill, declared maneuvers, theory's perceived help and narrated musical pleasure are achieved positives. Fatigue, finger injury reports, stopped sessions, objections to titles and questions about the purpose of gymnastics are equally real. Neither applause nor a prize supplies consent to a joke, further labor or publicity. The record's wanted imperfection also shows that technical optimization is not the only criterion of value. [A:L207–231; P:L439,L455]

**“The band's success establishes professional status.”** Normal selection and hidden reported praise/understood explanation support local achievement. Prize collection is prospective; a signed agency contract, permanent ensemble, income stream and whole observed live are absent. Kazusa explicitly denies releasing an album and wants a commissioned LP as memory. Public achievement is not weakened by refusing unsupported career certification. [A:L184,L204–205; P:L394,L439]

**“All variant and event contexts form a simple maturation ladder.”** Different assigned roles, broader skill and local confidence invite developmental comparison. Source chronology supports a festival interval and countdowns, not a universal ordering of variants or a sequential fusion of normal/hidden endings. Natsu's missed-parfait callback provides a limited explicit connection, while private rental loss and ongoing fatigue contradict total final cure. Local revision is adequate without manufacturing the missing calendar. [A:L237; P:L394,L492,L501]

**“Airi's quiet image is merely false.”** Her private disclosure differs from public optimism, and in041 a parenthetical apology does not publicly correct blame laid on Natsu. These are consequential contrary acts. Her real affection, founder parity, wanted skill, helpful feedback and local self-liking are not thereby falsified. An image can be incomplete and selectively protected without every gentle act becoming strategic deception. [A:L168–180,L197,L224–225]

**“Natsu's romantic proposals are invariably useful leadership.”** Scheduling, endurance, cleaning, reflection on temporary time and a simple lunch question support practical and receptive contributions. Gymnastics produce a completed maneuver of questioned purpose, stick-spinning has audience objections and future shared plans are not unanimously welcome. Her own uncertainty qualifies perfect-plan rhetoric. Generosity, oddity and local imposition belong in one bounded account. [P:L498–504; A:L202,L211–214,L228–231]

**“Yoshimi's irritation should be dismissed as comic personality.”** She contributes actual style choices and serious musical work; sincere appraisal, purpose and a limited audience matter to her. Casual assignment, embarrassment, ignored stop requests, continued encores and fatigue explain particular objections. Bright enjoyment and comedy remain real, while they cannot establish that every unwanted tease is privately welcomed. [P:L449–455,L473–475; A:L160,L166,L196]

**“Kazusa's imperfect record proves inadequate musical achievement.”** It contains early playing, missing parts and a cracked voice. She explicitly wants those imperfections as a memory of the first complete ensemble run and includes teacher's contribution. A professional best take would answer a different purpose. This defense of the object does not settle capture/distribution permission, make the staff labels secure or give the analyst acoustic credit. [P:L437–439]

**“Temporary means trivial or failed.”** The practice place ends, the future is unperformed and no permanent career is established. Local skill, selected expression, actual shared labor, a remembered record, grief and a statement of self-liking have nonetheless happened in the representation. Natsu's balance of photographs and living the moment specifically values finite time. The project's ending belongs to the argument as an achieved limit, rather than proof that its ordinary goods were never real. [P:L394,L439,L455; A:L180,L231]
